chapter: Family, marching bands and the tavern
title: Taking on the Sip 'n Beer in Altadena
summary: His niece asks him to hold the liquor license and he ends up owning the Altadena tavern, opening in 1965.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: That was about 1965.
Perhaps you had somewhat of a new role at that time? What did you venture into at that time, Mr. Blakeney?
Later on that year, later, I think around December, I got into a new venture.

My niece, who used to be club owner out in Milwaukee, wanted to open up a place out here, and she couldn't get a license for it because she got in trouble with the IRS back there, and she asked me, she said I want to open this place but I want you to get the license for me. I agreed, not knowing what I was in for.
She said I need some more money, I think if you lend me a thousand dollars I
think I can make it. So I said I'll let you have the thousand dollars.
This is your niece?
This is my niece. When it ended up, she needed five-thousand dollars. Well, still didn't know what I was in for, so she opened the place under my name, I'm the license holder.
What's the name of the club?
The Sip 'n Beer.
In Pasadena?
Altadena.
Not too far from here.
Right.

And later on I found out that I was responsible for anything that happened, if somebody breaks a leg they can sue you, because your name is on the license. I took it over from my niece and I ran it myself, because I was responsible and I had the most money in it.
December, 1961 we opened up, we had to do some remodeling and change around. All we did was open the doors and the people just lined up to come in, with no advertising or anything.
Was that '64 or '61?
'65. I was the first colored man in business up in that area.
In Altadena.
The only other business up there was a barber shop and after I opened up there came a chicken shop and a rib shop.
Like a typical black community.
In the meantime I kept on playing gigs, if anybody called me for a gig I'd make it, I'd get somebody to run the place for me.
